views.name: job_postings_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  jf.job_id,
  jf.company_id,
  jf.job_title_short,
  jf.job_title,
  jf.job_location,
  jf.job_via,
  jf.job_schedule_type,
  jf.job_work_from_home,
  jf.search_location,
  jf.job_posted_date,
  jf.job_no_degree_mention,
  jf.job_health_insurance,
  jf.job_country,
  jf.salary_rate,
  jf.salary_year_avg,
  jf.salary_hour_avg,
  jc.name AS name,
  jc.link AS link,
  jc.link_google AS link_google,
  jc.thumbnail AS thumbnail,
  sj.skill_id AS skill_id
FROM job_postings_fact AS jf
LEFT JOIN job_company AS jc
  ON jf.company_id = jc.company_id
LEFT JOIN skills_job_dim AS sj
  ON jf.job_id = sj.job_id
views.description: Denormalized row per job posting enriched with company and associated skill ids. Use this when analyzing job-level measures together with company metadata or skill associations. This preserves one row per job_id; if multiple skills exist per job this will produce multiple rows (one per skill association). | Use for: Job counts or salary averages by company, location, or skill; Join job postings to company metadata; Analyze distribution of job attributes for postings that list particular skills (after joining to skills_dim)

views.name: job_postings_company_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  company_id,
  COUNT(*) AS job_postings_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN job_work_from_home = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS work_from_home_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN job_no_degree_mention = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_degree_mention_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN job_health_insurance = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS health_insurance_count,
  AVG(salary_year_avg) AS avg_salary_year,
  AVG(salary_hour_avg) AS avg_salary_hour
FROM job_postings_fact
GROUP BY company_id
views.description: Aggregated metrics per company (one row per company_id) summarizing job posting counts and salary statistics. Use for company-level reporting and comparisons. This preserves company_id as the key. | Use for: Rank or compare companies by number of job postings; Correlate company-level average salary with prevalence of remote work or benefits mentions; Create dashboards showing company hiring activity

views.name: skills_with_type
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  skill_id,
  skills,
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(type) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE type
  END AS type
FROM skills_dim
views.description: Canonical skill dimension projection: one row per skill_id with skill text and type normalized to NULL when blank. Use when you need a clean skills lookup before joining to job associations. | Use for: Lookup skill names or filter jobs by skill type; Aggregate jobs by skill categories after joining skills_job_dim

views.name: alien_profile_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id,
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name,
  a.email,
  a.gender,
  a.type,
  a.birth_year,
  ad.age AS age,
  ad.favorite_food AS favorite_food,
  ad.feeding_frequency AS feeding_frequency,
  ad.aggressive AS aggressive,
  al.current_location AS current_location,
  al.state AS state,
  al.country AS country,
  al.occupation AS occupation
FROM aliens AS a
LEFT JOIN alien_data AS ad
  ON a.id = ad.id
LEFT JOIN aliens_location AS al
  ON ad.current_location = al.current_location
views.description: Denormalized alien profile combining core identity, location and detail attributes. One row per alien id. Useful for people-level analyses without needing to join separate tables each time. Preserves identity columns from aliens and denormalized attributes from related tables when available via left joins. | Use for: Profile aliens by location, age, or aggressive flag; Count aliens by country or occupation; Identify mismatches between denormalized alien_data and normalized aliens/aliens_location tables

views.name: cities_country_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.city_id,
  c.city_name,
  c.latitude,
  c.longitude,
  c.country_code_2,
  c.capital,
  c.population,
  c.insert_date,
  cc.country_id AS country_id,
  cc.country_name AS country_name,
  cc.country_code_3 AS country_code_3,
  cc.region AS region,
  cc.sub_region AS sub_region,
  cc.intermediate_region AS intermediate_region,
  cc.created_on AS created_on
FROM cities AS c
LEFT JOIN cities_countries AS cc
  ON LOWER(c.country_code_2) = LOWER(cc.country_code_2)
views.description: One row per city joined to its country metadata by country_code_2. Use for geolocation analyses combining city-level population/coordinates with country-level attributes. | Use for: Aggregate city populations by country or region; Map jobs or aliens to country/region via city; Filter capital cities and their country attributes

views.name: legislator_latest_term
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.id_bioguide,
  lt.term_number,
  lt.term_id,
  lt.term_type,
  lt.term_start,
  lt.term_end,
  lt.state,
  lt.district,
  lt.class,
  lt.party,
  lt.how,
  lt.url,
  lt.address,
  lt.phone,
  lt.fax,
  lt.contact_form,
  lt.office,
  lt.state_rank,
  lt.rss_url,
  lt.caucus
FROM (
  SELECT *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id_bioguide ORDER BY COALESCE(term_end, term_start) DESC) AS rn
  FROM legislators_terms
) AS lt
WHERE lt.rn = 1
views.description: Latest term per legislator id_bioguide based on term_end date. One row per id_bioguide representing the most recent term record. Useful for retrieving current state/district/party information. | Use for: Get current party/state/district for each legislator; Join latest term info back to legislator bio table

views.name: legislators_person
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.full_name,
  l.first_name,
  l.last_name,
  l.middle_name,
  l.nickname,
  l.suffix,
  l.other_names_end,
  l.other_names_middle,
  l.other_names_last,
  l.birthday,
  l.gender,
  l.id_bioguide,
  l.id_bioguide_previous_0,
  l.id_govtrack,
  l.id_icpsr,
  l.id_wikipedia,
  l.id_wikidata,
  l.id_google_entity_id,
  l.id_house_history,
  l.id_house_history_alternate,
  l.id_thomas,
  l.id_cspan,
  l.id_votesmart,
  l.id_lis,
  l.id_ballotpedia,
  l.id_opensecrets,
  l.id_fec_0,
  l.id_fec_1,
  l.id_fec_2,
  lt.term_id AS term_id,
  lt.term_start AS term_start,
  lt.term_end AS term_end,
  lt.state AS state,
  lt.district AS district,
  lt.party AS party
FROM legislators AS l
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id_bioguide ORDER BY COALESCE(term_end, term_start) DESC) AS rn
    FROM legislators_terms
  ) WHERE rn = 1
) AS lt
  ON l.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
views.description: One row per legislator (from legislators) with their latest term attributes joined in. Use for combined person+office analyses while preserving legislator identity columns. | Use for: List current legislators with contact/office info; Analyze legislator demographics by party or state
